questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consumer Movement' refers to.
questions.a: The consumer movement arose out of dissatisfaction of consumers regarding unfair trade practices like adulteration, false advertising, and black marketing, leading to organised efforts to protect and promote consumer interests.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consumer Movement'.
questions.a: The consumer movement is a collective effort to protect consumers from unfair trade practices and to ensure their rights are respected.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consumer Movement' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Consumer Movement

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consumer Rights' refers to.
questions.a: Consumer rights are a set of rights that protect consumers in the marketplace, including the right to safety, the right to be informed, the right to choose, the right to be heard, the right to seek redressal, and the right to consumer education.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consumer Rights'.
questions.a: Consumer rights protect buyers from exploitation and ensure they can make informed choices and seek justice when cheated.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consumer Rights' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Consumer Rights

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Right to Information' refers to.
questions.a: The right to information means a consumer has the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods or services so as to protect against unfair trade practices.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Right to Information'.
questions.a: Consumers must be given full information about a product so they can make an informed choice and avoid being cheated.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Right to Information' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Right to be Informed

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Right to Choose' refers to.
questions.a: The right to choose means a consumer has the right to choose from a variety of goods and services at competitive prices, and should not be forced to buy a particular product or brand.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Right to Choose'.
questions.a: Consumers must have access to a range of products at fair prices and must not be coerced into buying any one brand or item.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Right to Choose' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Right to Choose

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Right to Seek Redressal' refers to.
questions.a: The right to seek redressal means a consumer has the right to seek compensation or remedy against unfair trade practices, exploitation, or defective goods and services through consumer courts and forums.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Right to Seek Redressal'.
questions.a: Consumers can claim compensation and remedies for defective goods or unfair practices through a legal redressal system.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Right to Seek Redressal' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Right to Seek Redressal

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consumer Protection and COPRA' refers to.
questions.a: The Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) of 1986 is a law enacted by the Government of India to protect consumer rights, establish consumer councils and authorities, and set up a three-tier quasi-judicial system for consumer disputes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consumer Protection and COPRA'.
questions.a: COPRA provides a legal framework to protect consumer rights and a three-tier system of consumer courts for redressal of complaints.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consumer Protection and COPRA' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Consumer Protection Act, 1986

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consumer Courts and Forums' refers to.
questions.a: Consumer courts, also called consumer disputes redressal agencies, are quasi-judicial bodies set up under COPRA at three levels -- District Forum, State Commission and National Commission -- to hear and decide consumer complaints.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consumer Courts and Forums'.
questions.a: Consumer courts provide a simple, inexpensive and speedy mechanism for resolving disputes between consumers and sellers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consumer Courts and Forums' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Consumer Courts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Consumer Organisations' refers to.
questions.a: Consumer organisations and NGOs play an important role in creating consumer awareness, educating people about their rights, helping them file complaints, and pressurising the government for stronger consumer protection laws.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Consumer Organisations'.
questions.a: Consumer organisations spread awareness, help consumers seek redressal, and push for better laws to protect consumer interests.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of Consumer Organisations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Role of Consumer Organisations

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Standardisation and Quality Marks' refers to.
questions.a: Standardisation is the process of setting common standards for goods and services to ensure quality and safety. Quality marks like ISI, Agmark, Hallmark and ISO certify that a product meets the prescribed standards.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Standardisation and Quality Marks'.
questions.a: Standardisation and quality marks assure consumers that products meet specified standards of quality, safety and purity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Standardisation and Quality Marks' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Standardisation and Quality Marks
